title: Skills
teaser: Know-how the AI loads on demand

basics.say: Imagine a binder of recipe cards next to the AI: brand voice, weekly report, invoice check. Those are skills.
A skill is a packaged set of instructions – sometimes with files or scripts – for doing one kind of task well.
When a task comes in, like 'write this week's report', the AI pulls out the matching card and follows it.
The other cards stay on the shelf – the AI only sees a one-line label on each. It reads in full only the card it picks.
Skills let a team write its know-how down once and reuse it every time, the same way.

deeper.say: In practice, a skill is often a folder with a main instruction file. Its short description tells the AI when to use it.
Because only those short descriptions are read up front, you can install many skills without overloading the AI.
Skills and tools work together: a skill can explain how to use certain tools for a specific job.
Treat skills like any shared document: keep them up to date, and only install skills from sources you trust.

takeaway: A skill is reusable know-how the AI loads only when a task needs it.
